newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Most rivers in Romania are expected to recede in the coming 24 hours after floods at the weekend, but the rivers Ialomita and Prahova in southern Romania are expected to flow out of their beds, affecting several villages.
* The Romanian Red Cross society has distributed mineral water in the mountain resort of Breaza, after its water supplies were disrupted by heavy rain and land slides.
* The new road tax was enforced on Monday despite protests from drivers' unions and transport companies.

* The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has signed an accord to give Romania a $75 million loan, as part of a $190 million project for upgrading water supplies and drainage systems in 10 Romanian cities and towns including Arad, Cluj and Bacau.
The EU has granted an additional $35 million for the same project, with the Romanian government providing the rest.
* Government members met at the finance ministry headquarters to discuss last-minute details of the budget revision ahead of the government meeting on Tuesday.
* Interior Minister Gavril Dejeu is touring several central counties, where most of the Hungarian ethnic minority lives, to monitor places where bilingual street signs should be put up.
* Employees of the Astra Vagoane rail equipment maker have launched a warning strike over the SNCFR railway authority's failure to pay 118 billion lei worth of debts to the company.
